label: Theodore F. Stevens
narrative: Stevens supplied the bipartisan cover and the second half of the appropriations muscle. He had chaired Senate Appropriations from 1997 to 2005 and remained its most senior Republican in 2007, and his sign-off is what made the AAWSAP earmark a leadership consensus item rather than a Democratic Majority Leader's personal project. Reid has said Stevens had a personal interest in the subject dating to his service as a wartime pilot, an account that is in Reid's telling only. Stevens matters to the board structurally: the AAWSAP appropriation is a textbook case of the appropriations-leadership triad creating a classified program that the authorizing committees never saw, and Stevens is one third of that triad. He lost his seat in 2008 following a prosecution later vacated for government misconduct, and died in a plane crash in Alaska on 9 August 2010, while AAWSAP was still running.
